policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 6:4 reads 'Five golden tumors', and both candidates denote the same swellings: qere טְחֹרֵי and ketiv עפלי are the standard qere/ketiv pair for this word, rendered alike in English. The only mapped note is a hebrew_gloss ('Hebrew them.'), which is not a textual_variant note and cannot select a reading. Nothing in the English wording or an italicized supply distinguishes the two, so the unit is underdetermined and the qere base fallback carries the projection.

ASV 6:5 reads 'images of your tumors'; qere טְחֹרֵיכֶ֜ם and ketiv עפליכם are the same word-pair with the same sense and the same second-person plural suffix, so both yield 'your tumors' identically. No ASV note is mapped to this unit and no italicized supply bears on it, so the English does not distinguish a reading: underdetermined, with the qere base fallback retained.
